title: The Echo of Deep Time
gist: In an essay reprinted by Long Now, novelist Amitav Ghosh blames the planetary crisis on short-term timeframes such as elections, quarterly earnings and news cycles. He offers the Haudenosaunee Seventh Generation Principle as an alternative, noting it is increasingly codified in law (Ecuador's Rights of Nature, Attawapiskat First Nation filings), and casts the Future Library project as bringing it into the arts.

themes.theme: Short-termism as root of planetary crisis

insights.claim: Amitav Ghosh argues that the planetary crisis largely results from short timeframes such as two- or four-year election cycles, quarterly earnings targets and breaking-news media cycles.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Quarterly-earnings short-termism is named as a systemic driver of climate risk, feeding the case for long-horizon stewardship and ESG pressure.
insights.quote: two- or four-year elections, for example, or quarterly earnings targets, or media cycles that reward breaking news

insights.claim: Amitav Ghosh contends that art and literature are not exempt from short-term pressures, since instant online publishing pushes writers to chase emerging trends.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Shows that attention-economy short-termism reaches even cultural production, not just markets and politics.

insights.claim: The Seventh Generation Principle, rooted in Haudenosaunee (Iroquois Confederacy) tradition, requires that every decision be evaluated for its impact on people seven generations in the future.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: A ready-made intergenerational decision test that could inform long-duration asset stewardship and governance.
insights.quote: this philosophy demands that every decision made today must be evaluated for its impact on the people who will inhabit the earth seven generations into the future
insights.locator: What, then, might be an alternative

insights.claim: Under the Haudenosaunee Great Law of Peace, decisions like clearing a forest, signing a treaty or adopting a new technology must pass the test of whether they benefit the children of one's great-grandchildren, acting as a restraint on greed and expediency.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Applies the long-horizon test explicitly to technology adoption and resource extraction decisions.
insights.quote: Will this benefit the children of my great-grandchildren?
insights.locator: At its core, the Seventh Generation

insights.claim: The seven-generation planning horizon in Indigenous traditions is sustained through ritual, oral tradition, ceremony and place-based storytelling rather than formal rules alone.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Implies long-term commitments endure through culture and ritual, a design lesson for institutions seeking durability.
insights.quote: The seven-generation horizon is sustained through oral tradition, ceremony, and place-based storytelling.

themes.theme: Legal codification of future generations and nature

insights.claim: Seventh-generation-style principles are being codified in law, for example Ecuador's 2008 Constitution recognizing the Rights of Nature and the Attawapiskat First Nation citing the Seventh Generation Principle in court filings.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: Rights-of-nature and intergenerational legal claims are a growing litigation and regulatory risk for extractive and resource projects.
insights.quote: Ecuador’s 02008 Constitution recognized the Rights of Nature, and in recent years the Attawapiskat First Nation has cited the Seventh Generation Principle in court filings
insights.locator: Today, these principles are being codified

themes.theme: Future Library as long-term cultural practice

insights.claim: Amitav Ghosh, the 2025 Future Library Author of the Year, says the Future Library project effectively introduces the Seventh Generation Principle into literature and the arts by having writers address an audience not yet born.
insights.speaker: Long Now Foundation
insights.so_what: An example of cultural institutions building deliberately long-dated commitments.
insights.quote: the Future Library project is, in effect, introducing the Seventh Generation Principle into literature and the arts
